core.text: Carrier migration: move the function of selecting identities still needing acknowledgment from the bulk control’s pending display into a dispatcher arrangement guided by the recognition ledger. Use individual requests during N1’s stale display, then a safe bulk batch after clearing. The ledger guides selection; the existing server still delivers receipts.

Concrete candidate: validate N3,N4,N5,N6,N7,N8 at ticks 0,1,2,3,4,5. Request individual N2,N3,N4 at ticks 0,1,2; bulk at 4; individual N7 at 5 and N8 at 6. The bulk selects only N5,N6. Predicted deliveries are N2 at 1, N3 at 2, N4 at 3, N5 at 5, N6 at 6, N7 at 7, N8 at 8. Together with initial N1 recognition, this reaches eight registrations and eight recognitions using six actions.

Closest rival: keep the same validation order and six request ticks but use routine bulk every time. Separating probe: finite-model replay of both schedules, recording registrations, first recognitions, queued identities, duplicates, and pending clearing. Migration predicts eight recognitions; this rival predicts three, including initial N1, because repeated early entries occupy FIFO slots. These are derived predictions, not observed executions.

residue.text: Attack the new carrier’s dependency on registration order and delivery timing. Feasible stress variant: validate N8,N3,N4,N5,N6,N7 at ticks 0 through 5; request N2 at 0, N8 at 1, N3 at 2, bulk at 4, N6 at 5, N7 at 6. Early N8 fails at tick 2; its later bulk retry succeeds at 7, leaving N7 beyond the window. Predicted final recognition count is seven. This defeats success from ledger-guided selection alone.

Actor burden: six validations and six dispatcher actions; readable ledgers add no stipulated clerk labor. Maintaining the carrier means coordinating selections with boundary updates, preserving the safe batch, and checking queue order. No additional worker, action, server, configuration change, or endpoint repair is available.

Unknowns remain: origin of N1 delay, later sender adaptation, empirical network behavior, and global schedule optimality. No new demand occurs in this window. The schedule establishes finite-model feasibility only; it does not establish execution or future adaptation.

tension.account_a: Recognition-ledger selection carried by a coordinated request schedule can satisfy the fixed outcome.
tension.account_b: Dashboard-pending selection carried by routine bulk requests at those same boundaries can satisfy the fixed outcome.
tension.prediction_a: With the specified validation order, six requests produce eight distinct recognitions by boundary 9; the early-N8 stress variant produces seven.
tension.prediction_b: Replacing those six requests with bulk preserves eight recognitions. The separating replay predicts only three, defeating this account.
